text:
I think the oil in Transformer 1 at site MAIN may be losing its insulating strength, and I need to decide whether to plan an oil reconditioning before it becomes a real problem.

First, check dielectric_rigidity and interfacial_v between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000 for gaps. Tell me how many usable samples each has. Then forecast both 3 days ahead, one step per day, with an 80% prediction interval for each day, and tell me whether each one is heading down.

Separately, work out a health index and condition category from the latest oil sample. Also tell me whether hydrogen or acetylene in that sample suggests discharge activity in the weakened oil.

Only recommend reconditioning if both signals point to risk: at least one of the two forecasts is falling, and the health index is fair or worse. If that happens:
- Check the work order history on Transformer 1 for any oil filtration, degassing or regeneration in the past 12 months.
- If there was none, create one work order covering oil reconditioning plus a confirmatory oil quality test.
- Assign it to a technician who has worked on Transformer 1 before.
- If there was one, don't create a new work order. Give me its number and date, and say the oil may be degrading faster than expected.

If only one of the two signals points to risk, don't create anything. Recommend an oil quality retest instead and tell me which signal disagreed.

If either channel has fewer than 4 usable samples, don't run a model on it. Report its first-to-last change per day as a linear extrapolation with no interval, and say so.
characteristic_form: The agent should confirm the window with iot.stream_extent for Transformer 1 at MAIN and pull dielectric_rigidity and interfacial_v with iot.history over 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 to 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000. It should check completeness, either with tsfm.data_quality on the materialized series or by counting non-null values. For any channel with at least 4 usable samples, it should pick a forecaster with tsfm.find_models and run a 3-step forecast with 80% intervals using tsfm.run_recipe. For channels with fewer than 4 samples, it should report a linear first-to-last rate labelled as extrapolation. It should get the latest sample with iot.latest_reading and call fmsr.predict_health_index with hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, methane, co, co2, ethylene, ethane, acetylene, dbds, interfacial_v and dielectric_rigidity from that sample, and should not invent missing inputs. It should comment on hydrogen and acetylene as discharge indicators. The decision requires both a falling forecast and a health category of fair or worse. Only then should it call wo.list_workorders on Transformer 1 to look for oil treatment in the past 12 months. If there was none, it should call wo.generate_work_order for reconditioning plus a confirmatory test, then wo.assign_technician using a labor code taken from prior Transformer 1 work orders. If there was a recent treatment, it should create nothing and report that work order's number and date. If only one signal indicates risk, it should create no work order, recommend a retest and name the disagreeing signal.

text:
The last maintenance job on Transformer 1 at site MAIN was supposed to deal with the gassing, and I want to know whether it actually worked.

Find the most recently closed work order on Transformer 1. Give me its number, description, completion date, resolution notes and failure code, and tell me which fault it was meant to fix.

Then look at the oil samples taken after that date, within 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 to 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000. Use hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co. Screen hydrogen, acetylene and co for anomalous samples with a proper anomaly detection model rather than a fixed threshold. Separately, run a dissolved gas fault classification on the latest complete sample and compare its fault class with the fault the job was meant to fix.

Decide as follows:
- If both checks point to trouble, meaning at least one anomaly is flagged and the classification still shows the same fault or a higher-energy one, call the fix ineffective. Create a priority 2 corrective follow-up work order that references the original work order number, and code it with the closest failure code from our catalog.
- If only one of the two checks points to trouble, don't create a corrective job. Recommend a confirmatory oil resample within 7 days and say which check disagreed.
- If neither points to trouble, say the fix appears to have held.

If the closed job was oil filtration, degassing or regeneration, the gas levels will have been reset. In that case, judge the result on the rate of change after the job, not on absolute levels, and say you did so.

If no work order on Transformer 1 was closed before or during the window, say so, use all samples in the window, and give only the classification and anomaly result without a verdict on any fix. If fewer than 4 samples fall after the completion date, skip the anomaly model and compare the first and last post-job values instead.
characteristic_form: The agent should call wo.list_workorders filtered to asset Transformer 1 at MAIN, identify the most recently closed work order, and read its completion date, resolution notes and failure code from the returned work order details. It should confirm the post-job sample range with iot.stream_extent and pull hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co with iot.history, restricted to samples after the completion date and within 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 to 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000. If at least 4 samples remain, it should select a detector with tsfm.find_models(task_id='tsfm_anomaly_detection') and screen hydrogen, acetylene and co with tsfm.run_recipe. Otherwise it should compare first and last values. It should call fmsr.interpret_dga on the latest complete sample and compare the IEC class with the fault the original job targeted. The job counts as ineffective only when both the anomaly check and the classification indicate trouble. In that case it should look up a code with wo.get_failure_codes and create a priority 2 follow-up with wo.generate_work_order that references the original work order. If the two checks disagree, it should recommend a resample within 7 days and create no corrective order. For filtration or degassing jobs, it should judge on post-job rates rather than absolute levels. If no closed work order exists, it should report classification and anomaly results only, with no verdict on a fix.

text:
I want to set the next oil sampling date for Transformer 1 at site MAIN based on how fast the gases are actually growing, not on a fixed calendar.

Using the samples between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, work out TDCG for every sample. Use only hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co, and leave out co2, oxygen and nitrogen. Give me the TDCG rate in ppm/day between the first and last sample, and name the gas that contributes most to the increase.

Before trusting that rate, screen the six gases for anomalous samples. If a single anomalous sample is driving the rise, recompute the rate without it and show me both numbers.

Set the interval with this rule:
- Under 10 ppm/day: next sample in 90 days.
- 10 to 30 ppm/day: next sample in 30 days.
- Above 30 ppm/day: next sample in 7 days.

If the rate with and without the anomalous sample lands in different bands, don't escalate on the higher one. Use the lower band's interval and add a confirmatory resample within 7 days to settle it.

Also run a fault classification on the latest complete sample. If it comes back D1, D2 or T3, use 7 days no matter what the rate says.

Then check open work orders on Transformer 1. If a sampling job is already open, don't create another. Tell me its number and date, and whether it should move earlier. Otherwise, pick the first day on or after the target date where MAIN has fewer than 3 scheduled work orders, create the sampling work order for that day, and assign a technician who has sampled Transformer 1 before.

If fewer than two samples in the window have all six gases, say the rate can't be computed. In that case, base the interval on the classification alone: 7 days for D1, D2 or T3, and 30 days otherwise.
characteristic_form: The agent should confirm the window with iot.stream_extent for Transformer 1 at MAIN and pull the six combustible gases with iot.history over 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 to 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000. It should compute per-sample TDCG, excluding co2, oxygen and nitrogen, calculate the first-to-last rate in ppm/day, and name the largest contributing gas. It should screen the gases for anomalies using tsfm.find_models(task_id='tsfm_anomaly_detection') and tsfm.run_recipe, and recompute the rate without any single dominant anomalous sample. It should call fmsr.interpret_dga on the latest complete sample. The rate band sets the interval (90, 30 or 7 days). If the two rates fall in different bands, the lower band's interval applies plus a confirmatory resample. A D1, D2 or T3 class overrides the interval to 7 days. It should check wo.list_workorders for an existing open sampling job and avoid duplicating it. It should use wo.get_schedule_calendar at MAIN to find the first day on or after the target date with fewer than 3 scheduled work orders, then call wo.generate_work_order and wo.assign_technician with a labor code from prior Transformer 1 sampling work. If fewer than two complete samples exist, it should report that the rate is not computable and base the interval on the classification alone.

text:
We're short on crews this month, and I'd like to push the next planned job on Transformer 1 at site MAIN back by 30 days. Tell me whether that's safe.

Find the open or pending-approval work order on Transformer 1 with the earliest scheduled date. Give me its number, description, priority and scheduled date. If it's an oil sampling or DGA job, don't defer it under any circumstances. Just say why.

Otherwise, build two separate pieces of evidence:
1. Using the samples between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, forecast hydrogen, ethylene and acetylene 7 days ahead from the last sample, with an 80% upper bound. Compare the upper bounds with the IEEE C57.104 Condition 1 limits of 100 ppm for hydrogen, 50 ppm for ethylene and 1 ppm for acetylene.
2. Run a dissolved gas fault classification on the latest complete sample, using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene.

Decide as follows:
- Approve the deferral only if no upper bound crosses its limit and the class is not D1, D2 or T3. In that case, find a day about 30 days after the current scheduled date where MAIN has fewer than 3 scheduled work orders. Add a note to the work order with the proposed new date and the evidence behind it.
- If both pieces of evidence point to risk, keep the original date. Raise the priority to 1 if acetylene is the gas crossing its limit.
- If they disagree, keep the original date, don't change the priority, and recommend a confirmatory oil resample before revisiting the deferral.

If any of the three gases has fewer than 4 usable samples, don't model it. Project its last value forward 7 days using the average daily change between the first and last samples, and label it as a linear extrapolation with no interval.
characteristic_form: The agent should call wo.list_workorders for Transformer 1 at MAIN with status OPEN and APPROVED_PENDING, and select the work order with the earliest scheduled date. If that work order is a sampling or DGA job, the agent should refuse the deferral. Otherwise it should pull hydrogen, ethylene and acetylene with iot.history over 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 to 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, check sample counts, and for series with at least 4 usable samples select a model with tsfm.find_models and run a 7-day forecast with 80% intervals via tsfm.run_recipe. Series with fewer samples get a labelled linear extrapolation. It should compare the upper bounds with the 100, 50 and 1 ppm limits. It should call fmsr.interpret_dga on the latest complete sample, taken from iot.latest_reading or iot.history. Deferral is allowed only when both signals are benign. In that case it should use wo.get_schedule_calendar to find a date about 30 days later with fewer than 3 scheduled work orders and record it with wo.update_workorder notes. If both signals indicate risk, it should keep the date and raise the priority to 1 via wo.update_workorder if acetylene crosses its limit. If the signals disagree, it should keep the date and priority unchanged and recommend a resample.

text:
Oxygen and nitrogen in Transformer 1's oil at site MAIN might be creeping up, which could mean a leaking gasket or a breather or conservator problem letting air in. I'd like to know before the oil oxidizes.

Between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, give me the first and last values of oxygen and nitrogen, and the daily change for each. Then look at how they move together with top-oil temperature (oti) and ambient (ati). I want to know whether the rise simply follows temperature swings, as normal thermal breathing would, or happens independently of them.

Separately, check whether the oil is already suffering from oxidation:
- Look at the trend in interfacial_v.
- Work out the CO2/CO ratio at the last sample.
- Get a health index and condition category from the latest sample.

Treat a seal leak as likely only if oxygen and nitrogen both rose and the rise is not explained by temperature. If so, first check open work orders on Transformer 1 for any existing gasket, breather or conservator inspection. If one exists, give me its number and don't duplicate it. Otherwise, create an inspection work order covering gaskets, the conservator and the breather. Make it priority 2 if interfacial_v fell over the window or the health index is fair or worse, and priority 3 otherwise.

If only one of the two gases rose, or the rise tracks temperature, don't create a work order. Recommend a resample taken with a gas-tight syringe to rule out sampling contamination, and say which condition wasn't met.

If oxygen has no data in the window, say that air ingress can't be properly assessed. Give a nitrogen-only view labelled low confidence, and don't create a work order.
characteristic_form: The agent should confirm the window with iot.stream_extent for Transformer 1 at MAIN and retrieve oxygen, nitrogen, oti, ati, interfacial_v, co and co2 with iot.history over 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 to 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000. It may use iot.sensor_stats for summaries. It should report first and last values and daily changes for oxygen and nitrogen. It should materialize the series and run tsfm.profile_series on the dissolved-air group (oxygen, nitrogen) alongside the temperature group (oti, ati) to judge whether the gas rise tracks temperature. It should compute the CO2/CO ratio at the last sample and the interfacial_v trend, and call fmsr.predict_health_index with the latest sample values from iot.latest_reading. A seal leak is concluded only when both gases rose and the rise is independent of temperature. The agent should then check wo.list_workorders for existing seal, breather or conservator inspections before calling wo.generate_work_order. The work order is priority 2 if interfacial_v fell or the health index is fair or worse, and priority 3 otherwise. If the conditions are not met, the agent should create no work order and recommend a gas-tight resample. If oxygen has no data, it should give a low-confidence nitrogen-only assessment and create no work order.

text:
I'm starting to suspect the cooling on Transformer 1 at site MAIN, such as fans, radiators or oil pumps, rather than anything inside the tank. Check this for me before I send a crew out.

Between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, work out the top-oil rise over ambient (oti minus ati) for every sample. For each sample, give it alongside the total phase current (il1 + il2 + il3). Then tell me whether the rise is climbing while the current stays roughly flat, meaning total current changes by less than 10% from first to last sample. That pattern points to lost cooling capacity rather than load.

Forecast the oti-minus-ati rise 2 days ahead, one step per day, with an 80% upper bound. Then check whether oti itself would get closer to its alarm reading (oti_a) than it is today.

Separately, run a dissolved gas fault classification on the latest complete sample using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene. This tells me whether there's an internal thermal fault instead.

Decide as follows:
- Cooling problem: the rise is climbing with flat current, and the gas class is not T2, T3, D1 or D2. First check open work orders on Transformer 1 for an existing cooling system inspection. If there's none, create one at priority 3, or priority 2 if the forecast upper bound brings oti within 5 °C of oti_a.
- Internal fault: the gas class is T2, T3, D1 or D2. Don't raise a cooling work order. Tell me the rise pattern is more likely a symptom of an internal fault and recommend a confirmatory oil resample.
- Rise doesn't climb: say that cooling looks healthy and create nothing.

If oti or ati has fewer than 4 non-null samples, don't forecast. Report the first-to-last change in the rise per day as a linear extrapolation with no interval.
characteristic_form: Coordinated iot, tsfm, fmsr and wo workflow. The agent confirms the window with iot.stream_extent and retrieves oti, ati, oti_a, il1, il2 and il3 per sample with iot.history over 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 to 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000. It computes the oti minus ati rise and the total phase current for each sample, and tests whether current changed by less than 10% while the rise increased. It checks series completeness with tsfm.data_quality, selects a forecaster with tsfm.find_models, and runs a 2-step forecast with an 80% interval via tsfm.run_recipe on the derived rise. If fewer than 4 non-null samples exist, it uses a linear extrapolation with no interval. It gets the latest complete five-gas sample with iot.latest_reading or iot.history and classifies it with fmsr.interpret_dga. Decision logic: when the rise climbs under flat load and the class is not T2, T3, D1 or D2, the agent calls wo.list_workorders for Transformer 1 to avoid duplicates. It then creates a cooling-inspection work order with wo.generate_work_order at priority 3, or priority 2 if the forecast upper bound on oti comes within 5 °C of oti_a. If the class is T2, T3, D1 or D2, it creates no cooling work order and recommends a resample. If the rise does not climb, it creates nothing. The answer reports the per-sample rise, the forecast, the gas class and the decision.

text:
The neutral current on Transformer 1 at site MAIN looks higher than I'd expect. I want to know if we have a phase imbalance that's heating something inside the unit.

Between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, give me the mean of il1, il2, il3 and inut. For each sample, work out the current imbalance as the largest deviation of any phase from the three-phase average, in percent. Screen inut together with the three phase currents for anomalous samples using a proper anomaly detection model, and list any flagged timestamps.

Then run a dissolved gas fault classification on the oil sample nearest to the worst-imbalance timestamp, using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene. Check co from that same sample to see whether the paper is involved.

Decide as follows:
- Escalate only if two things are both true: imbalance exceeds 10% in at least one sample or inut is flagged anomalous, and the gas class is thermal (T1, T2 or T3). In that case, look up the failure code in our catalog that best fits a core or winding thermal fault. Check open work orders on Transformer 1 so you don't duplicate one. Then create a priority 2 work order for a load-balance review and an electrical test, coded with that failure code.
- If only the electrical evidence or only the gas evidence points to a problem, don't create a work order. Recommend a confirmatory oil resample and say which side disagreed.

Only use samples where all four current channels are non-null. If fewer than 4 such samples remain, skip the anomaly model and use the 10% imbalance rule on its own.
characteristic_form: Coordinated iot, tsfm, fmsr and wo workflow. The agent retrieves il1, il2, il3 and inut over 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 to 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000 with iot.history and gets their means with iot.sensor_stats. It computes the per-sample imbalance percentage and keeps only samples where all four channels are non-null. It selects a detector with tsfm.find_models(task_id='tsfm_anomaly_detection') and runs it with tsfm.run_recipe on inut and the phase currents; if fewer than 4 complete samples exist, it skips the model and applies the 10% rule alone. It pulls the five gases and co nearest the worst-imbalance timestamp with iot.history and classifies them with fmsr.interpret_dga. It escalates only if the electrical evidence (imbalance above 10% or an anomalous inut) and a thermal T1, T2 or T3 class agree. In that case it calls wo.get_failure_codes to choose a core or winding thermal code and wo.list_workorders to check for duplicates. It then creates a priority 2 work order with wo.generate_work_order carrying that failure code. If the two sides disagree, it creates no work order, recommends a resample and names the disagreeing side.

text:
I'm writing the shift handover for Transformer 1 at site MAIN, and I don't want to hand over a diagnosis based on old oil data.

First, tell me when the newest oil sample was taken and how old it is in days. Give me the full data span and the number of samples.

Then give me two findings from the latest complete sample:
- A dissolved gas fault classification from hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene.
- A health index and condition category, using those five gases plus co, co2, oxygen, nitrogen, dbds, interfacial_v and dielectric_rigidity.

Next, list every open and pending-approval work order on Transformer 1 with its number, description, priority and scheduled date.

Decide as follows:
- If the newest sample is more than 30 days old, treat both findings as not current. Label them 'stale' in the handover.
- In that case, if no open work order already covers oil sampling, create one. Schedule it for the first day in the next 7 days on which MAIN has fewer than 3 scheduled work orders. Make it priority 2 if the health index is fair or worse or the class is D1, D2 or T3, and priority 3 otherwise.
- If the sample is 30 days old or less, don't create anything. Just summarize the findings.

Finish with a short handover note of no more than five lines.

If the health index can't be computed because an input is missing, name the missing input. Base the priority on the gas classification alone, and don't estimate the missing value.
characteristic_form: Coordinated iot, fmsr and wo workflow. The agent calls iot.latest_reading for Transformer 1 at MAIN to get the newest timestamp and age_seconds, which it converts to days. It calls iot.stream_extent for the data span and record count. It retrieves the latest complete sample, falling back to iot.history if fields are null, and runs fmsr.interpret_dga on the five fault gases and fmsr.predict_health_index on the full input set. If an input is missing, it names it and uses the DGA class alone. It lists open and pending work orders with wo.list_workorders for Transformer 1. If the sample is more than 30 days old and no sampling work order exists, it checks wo.get_schedule_calendar for MAIN over the next 7 days to find the first day with fewer than 3 scheduled work orders. It then creates a sampling work order with wo.generate_work_order at priority 2 if the health index is fair or worse or the class is D1, D2 or T3, and priority 3 otherwise. The output includes sample age, span, the class, the health index, the work order list, the staleness verdict, the actions taken and a handover note of no more than five lines.

text:
I don't want a single algorithm deciding whether Transformer 1 at site MAIN had a gassing event. Get a second opinion from a different method.

Between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, screen hydrogen and ethylene with two different anomaly detection models from our catalog. For each model and each gas, list the flagged timestamps, and tell me where the two models agree. If one of the models can't load or run, swap in the next candidate and tell me which one you replaced.

For any timestamp both models flag on at least one gas, run a dissolved gas fault classification on that sample using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene.

Decide as follows:
- If both models agree on a timestamp and its class is D1, D2, T2 or T3, do the following:
  - Check open work orders on Transformer 1 for an existing oil retest.
  - If there's none, create a priority 2 confirmatory oil sample work order that lists the agreed timestamps and fault class in the notes.
  - Assign it to the technician with the fewest open work orders at MAIN.
- If the models disagree, or they agree but the class is PD or T1, don't create a work order. Tell me which timestamps were disputed and recommend watching the next routine sample.
- If neither model flags anything, say the window looks stable.

If either gas has fewer than 4 non-null samples, don't run the models on it. Flag any sample more than 50% above that gas's window mean as a manual outlier, and treat it as a single-method result that can't trigger a work order.
characteristic_form: Coordinated iot, tsfm, fmsr and wo workflow. The agent retrieves hydrogen and ethylene over 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 to 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000 with iot.history and checks non-null counts with tsfm.data_quality. It shortlists at least two detectors with tsfm.find_models(task_id='tsfm_anomaly_detection') and runs each with tsfm.run_recipe on both gases; if a model fails to load or run, it substitutes the next candidate from the tsfm.find_models shortlist and reports the swap. It compares the flagged timestamps across models. For timestamps both models flag, it pulls the five gases with iot.history and classifies them with fmsr.interpret_dga. If the models agree and the class is D1, D2, T2 or T3, it checks wo.list_workorders for an existing retest. If none exists, it creates one with wo.generate_work_order at priority 2 and assigns it with wo.assign_technician to the technician with the fewest open work orders at MAIN, determined from wo.list_workorders. Disagreement between the models, or a PD or T1 class, produces no work order. For a gas with fewer than 4 samples, the agent uses a manual rule of more than 50% above its mean from iot.sensor_stats, which cannot trigger a work order on its own.

text:
Hydrogen seems to dominate the gases in Transformer 1 at site MAIN, and I'm worried about partial discharge eating into weakened oil. I'd like electrical PD testing arranged properly, but only if the evidence holds up.

Build three findings in order.

1. Using the latest complete sample, run a dissolved gas fault classification from hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene. Tell me hydrogen's share of the five-gas total.

2. Between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, give me the first and last values of dielectric_rigidity and interfacial_v. Tell me whether each one fell.

3. Forecast hydrogen 3 days ahead, one step per day, with an 80% upper bound. Tell me whether the upper bound crosses 100 ppm on any day.

Decide as follows:
- Arrange PD testing only if the class comes back PD or D1, and at least one of the other two findings also points to risk: the oil strength fell, or the forecast crosses 100 ppm.
- In that case, check open work orders on Transformer 1 for existing electrical or PD testing. If there's none, create one coded with the closest failure code for partial discharge from our catalog. Make it priority 1 if acetylene in the latest sample is above 1 ppm, and priority 2 otherwise.
- Assign it to a technician who has worked on Transformer 1 before. Give it a start date in the next 10 days that avoids any day with 3 or more scheduled work orders at MAIN.
- If the class isn't PD or D1, or neither supporting finding points to risk, don't book testing. Recommend a confirmatory oil resample and say which finding held it back.

If hydrogen has fewer than 4 usable samples, don't model it. Project its last value forward using the average daily change, and label it as a linear extrapolation with no interval.
characteristic_form: Coordinated iot, fmsr, tsfm and wo workflow. The agent gets the latest complete five-gas sample with iot.latest_reading, falling back to iot.history, computes hydrogen's share, and classifies the sample with fmsr.interpret_dga. It retrieves dielectric_rigidity and interfacial_v over 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 to 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000 with iot.history or iot.sensor_stats and reports the first and last values and their direction. It checks hydrogen completeness with tsfm.data_quality, picks a model with tsfm.find_models, and forecasts 3 steps with an 80% interval via tsfm.run_recipe. If hydrogen has fewer than 4 samples, it uses a linear extrapolation instead. Testing is booked only if the class is PD or D1 and at least one supporting finding (falling oil strength or a forecast crossing 100 ppm) agrees. In that case the agent checks wo.list_workorders for existing testing and prior Transformer 1 technicians, and selects a partial discharge code with wo.get_failure_codes. It creates the work order with wo.generate_work_order at priority 1 if acetylene is above 1 ppm and priority 2 otherwise. It finds a start date in the next 10 days with fewer than 3 scheduled work orders using wo.get_schedule_calendar, and assigns a technician with Transformer 1 history using wo.assign_technician. Otherwise it recommends a resample and names the finding that held the booking back.

text:
There's an open corrective work order on Transformer 1 at site MAIN for the gassing problem, and the crew says the unit has settled down. I want to check that before we close it.

Find the open corrective work order on Transformer 1 that relates to gassing, discharge, overheating or oil treatment. Give me its number, description, priority, failure code and assigned technician. If there's more than one, work with the oldest and list the rest.

Then build two separate findings from the samples between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000:
1. Screen hydrogen, ethylene and acetylene for anomalous samples with a proper anomaly detection model. List any flagged timestamps with their values.
2. Run a dissolved gas fault classification on the first and the last complete sample, using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene. Tell me whether the class stayed the same, moved to a lower-energy or lower-temperature fault, or got worse.

Decide as follows:
- Close the work order only if both findings say it's calm: nothing is flagged in the last two samples, and the last class is the same as or milder than the first. Put both findings in the resolution notes and keep the existing failure code.
- If exactly one finding points to trouble, don't close it. Add a note saying which check disagreed, and recommend a confirmatory oil resample within 7 days.
- If both findings point to trouble, keep it open and raise its priority by one level, but not above 1.

Count a sample as complete only if all five gases are non-null. If any of the three screened gases has fewer than 4 non-null samples, skip the model for that gas and flag any sample more than 50% above the gas's window mean as a manual outlier. If there's no matching open work order at all, say so, report both findings, and don't create anything.
characteristic_form: The agent calls wo.list_workorders filtered to Transformer 1 at MAIN with status OPEN and picks the oldest corrective work order related to gassing, discharge, overheating or oil treatment, using wo.get_workorder for details. It uses iot.stream_extent and iot.history for hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene over 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 to 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000 and identifies the first and last complete samples. It checks the series with tsfm.data_quality, selects a detector with tsfm.find_models(task_id='tsfm_anomaly_detection'), and runs tsfm.run_recipe on hydrogen, ethylene and acetylene. Any gas with fewer than 4 non-null samples falls back to a manual >50%-above-mean outlier check. It calls fmsr.interpret_dga on the first and last complete samples and compares the classes by energy and temperature. Decision logic: the work order is closed with wo.close_workorder, with resolution notes citing both findings and the existing failure code kept, only when there are no anomalies in the last two samples and the class is stable or milder. If exactly one finding shows trouble, wo.update_workorder adds a note naming the dissenting check and a resample within 7 days is recommended. If both show trouble, wo.update_workorder raises the priority by one level, capped at 1. If no matching work order exists, the agent reports the findings and creates nothing.

text:
I have a feeling we keep fixing the same fault on Transformer 1 at site MAIN without ever getting to the root cause. Check that for me.

Pull all closed work orders on Transformer 1 with their number, description, completion date and failure code. Use our failure code catalog to map each one to a transformer fault type: partial discharge, low-energy arcing, high-energy arcing, oil overheating, core or winding thermal fault, tap changer wear, moisture ingress, cellulose ageing or oil dielectric degradation.

Then work out what the transformer is doing now. Run a dissolved gas fault classification on the latest complete sample between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000 using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene, and use co from the same sample to check whether the paper is involved. Map that result to the same list of fault types.

Call it a recurring fault only if at least two closed work orders map to the same fault type the gases show today.

If it's recurring:
- Check open work orders on Transformer 1 for an existing root cause investigation or manufacturer referral. If there is one, give me its number and don't duplicate it.
- Otherwise, create a priority 2 root cause investigation work order. List the earlier work order numbers in the notes, add a note to notify the manufacturer, and code it with the matching failure code.

If only one earlier job matches, don't create anything. Recommend a confirmatory oil resample and say that one repeat isn't enough to call a pattern. If none match, say today's fault looks new.

If a closed work order has no failure code, map it from its description and mark it as inferred. Inferred matches can support a recurrence but can't be the only basis for one. If the latest sample is missing any of the five gases, use the most recent complete sample and give its timestamp.
characteristic_form: The agent calls wo.list_workorders for Transformer 1 at MAIN, including closed work orders, and wo.get_failure_codes to read the catalog. It maps each closed work order to a transformer fault type, marking mappings inferred from the description when no code exists. It uses iot.history (or iot.latest_reading) over 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 to 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000 to find the latest complete sample, falling back to the most recent complete sample if needed. It calls fmsr.interpret_dga with hydrogen, methane, acetylene, ethylene and ethane, checks co for paper involvement, and may use fmsr.get_failure_modes to align fault names. Recurrence requires at least two closed work orders matching the current fault type, and at least one of them must be code-based rather than inferred. If recurrence holds and no open root cause or manufacturer referral exists (checked via wo.list_workorders with status OPEN), wo.generate_work_order creates a priority 2 root cause investigation citing the prior work order numbers, with a manufacturer notification note and the matching failure code. With one match, the agent recommends a resample only. With zero matches, it reports a new fault.

text:
Ethylene in Transformer 1's oil at site MAIN looks to be pulling ahead of ethane, and I'm worried a low-temperature thermal fault is turning into a hot one.

For every sample between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, work out the ethylene-to-ethane ratio. Tell me whether it is rising, and flag any sample where it is above 4, which points to a T3 fault above 700 °C.

Check both gases for gaps first. Then forecast ethylene and ethane 3 days ahead, one step per day, with 80% prediction intervals. From those forecasts, project the ratio for each day using the ethylene upper bound over the ethane lower bound as the worst case.

Separately, run a dissolved gas fault classification on the latest complete sample using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene, and tell me whether acetylene is above 1 ppm.

Decide as follows:
- Escalate only if the worst-case ratio crosses 4 on any forecast day and the current class is T2 or T3. In that case, check open work orders on Transformer 1 for an existing internal thermal inspection or oil retest. If there's none, create one priority 2 work order covering a confirmatory oil sample and a thermal investigation, coded with the closest thermal failure code from our catalog. Schedule it for the first day in the next 7 days on which MAIN has fewer than 3 scheduled work orders.
- If only one of the two signals points to a hot fault, don't create anything. Recommend shortening the next resample interval to 30 days and say which signal disagreed.
- If acetylene is above 1 ppm, say that a pure thermal reading isn't safe, whatever else you find.

Skip any sample where ethane is zero or null when working out the ratio. If either gas has fewer than 4 usable samples, don't model it. Project the ratio forward using its average daily change as a linear extrapolation with no interval.
characteristic_form: The agent retrieves ethylene, ethane, hydrogen, methane and acetylene for Transformer 1 at MAIN with iot.stream_extent and iot.history over 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 to 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000. It computes C2H4/C2H6 per sample, skipping zero or null ethane, and flags ratios above 4. It checks gaps with tsfm.data_quality, picks a forecaster with tsfm.find_models(task_id='tsfm_forecasting'), and runs tsfm.run_recipe with a 3-step horizon and 80% conformal intervals on ethylene and ethane. Gases with fewer than 4 usable samples fall back to linear extrapolation of the ratio. The worst-case ratio is the ethylene upper bound over the ethane lower bound. It calls fmsr.interpret_dga on the latest complete sample and flags acetylene above 1 ppm as a caveat. Escalation requires both a worst-case ratio above 4 and a T2 or T3 class. In that case the agent checks wo.list_workorders for an open thermal inspection or retest, reads wo.get_failure_codes, picks a date with wo.get_schedule_calendar (first day in the next 7 with fewer than 3 scheduled work orders), and creates a priority 2 work order with wo.generate_work_order. With a single signal, it recommends a 30-day resample interval and names the disagreeing signal.

text:
My engineers disagree about whether the gassing in Transformer 1 at site MAIN is driven by load or by a fault that gasses no matter what the load is. Settle it with the data.

Between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, characterize how two groups move together: the fault gases (hydrogen, methane, ethylene and co) and the loading channels (il1, il2, il3 and inut). For each sample, give me the total phase current and the sum of the four gases. Tell me whether the gas sum rises in the same samples where current rises.

Separately, run a dissolved gas fault classification on the latest complete sample using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene. Also tell me whether top-oil temperature (oti) got close to its alarm reading (oti_a) at the highest-current sample.

Decide as follows:
- Call it load-driven only if the gases track current and the class is T1 or T2. In that case, don't create an inspection. Recommend a loading limit, and add a note about it to any open oil sampling work order on Transformer 1. If there's no such work order, say so.
- Call it a load-independent fault if the gases rise while current stays within 10% of its first value, or the class is PD, D1, D2 or T3. In that case, check open work orders on Transformer 1 for an existing internal inspection. If there's none, create a priority 2 inspection work order with the class and the gas trend in the notes.
- If neither case fits cleanly, create nothing. Recommend a confirmatory resample and explain the conflict.

Only use samples where all four current channels and all four gases are non-null. If fewer than 3 such samples remain, say that the correlation can't be judged, and base the decision on the gas classification alone.
characteristic_form: The agent uses iot.installed_sensors and iot.history for Transformer 1 at MAIN over 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 to 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000 to get hydrogen, methane, ethylene, co, il1, il2, il3, inut, oti and oti_a, keeping only samples where all eight gas and current channels are complete. It runs tsfm.characterize_series with groups {gases: [hydrogen, methane, ethylene, co], load: [il1, il2, il3, inut]} to describe how the groups co-move, and reports per-sample total current and gas sum. It calls fmsr.interpret_dga on the latest complete sample and checks oti against oti_a at the peak-current sample. Load-driven requires gases tracking current plus a T1 or T2 class. In that case the agent adds a loading-limit note with wo.update_workorder to an open sampling work order found via wo.list_workorders, or reports that none exists. Load-independent is triggered by gas rise with current within 10% of its first value, or by a PD, D1, D2 or T3 class. In that case, after checking open work orders, it creates a priority 2 inspection with wo.generate_work_order. Mixed evidence leads to a resample recommendation. With fewer than 3 complete samples, the correlation is declared unjudgeable and the decision uses fmsr.interpret_dga alone.

text:
I think we're over-sampling Transformer 1 at site MAIN, and I'd like to free up crew time if the oil is genuinely stable.

First, list every open and pending-approval oil sampling or DGA work order on Transformer 1 over the next 90 days, with its number, scheduled date and assigned technician.

Then build two findings from the samples between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000:
1. TDCG at the first and last complete sample, using only hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co, with the IEEE C57.104 condition for each. Condition 1 is up to 720 ppm, Condition 2 is 721 to 1920, Condition 3 is 1921 to 4630, and Condition 4 is above 4630. Also give me the TDCG rate in ppm/day.
2. A forecast of TDCG 7 days ahead from the last sample, with an 80% upper bound.

Treat the oil as stable only if both samples are Condition 1, the rate is under 10 ppm/day, and the forecast upper bound stays under 720 ppm.

If it's stable:
- Keep only the earliest sampling job in each 90-day block.
- Cancel the others, citing the kept work order number and the evidence in the reason.
- Never cancel a job that is priority 1 or that mentions acetylene or arcing.

If any of the three conditions fails, cancel nothing. Tell me which condition failed and whether the current schedule is dense enough for that condition level.

Finish with a table of each sampling job and whether it was kept or cancelled. If fewer than two complete samples exist, don't forecast, cancel nothing, and say the stability can't be shown.
characteristic_form: The agent calls wo.list_workorders for Transformer 1 at MAIN with OPEN and APPROVED_PENDING statuses and wo.get_schedule_calendar for the next 90 days to identify oil sampling and DGA jobs. It uses iot.stream_extent and iot.history for hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co over 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 to 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000 to compute TDCG at the first and last complete samples, excluding co2, oxygen and nitrogen, maps each to the IEEE condition limits, and computes ppm/day. It runs tsfm.data_quality, selects a forecaster with tsfm.find_models, and forecasts the per-sample TDCG series 7 steps ahead with an 80% interval via tsfm.run_recipe. Stability requires Condition 1 at both samples, a rate below 10 ppm/day, and a forecast upper bound below 720 ppm. If stable, the agent keeps the earliest job per 90-day block and calls wo.cancel_workorder on the others with a reason citing the kept work order and the evidence. It never cancels priority 1 jobs or jobs mentioning acetylene or arcing. Otherwise it cancels nothing and names the failed condition. With fewer than two complete samples, it skips the forecast and cancels nothing. fmsr.interpret_dga may optionally support the stability judgement.

text:
One of the recent oil samples from Transformer 1 at site MAIN shows a jump in hydrogen. Before anyone acts on it, I want to rule out a bad sample. A sample that picked up air during handling usually shows oxygen and nitrogen jumping at the same time.

Between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, screen hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen for anomalous samples with a proper anomaly detection model, not a fixed threshold. For each gas, list the flagged timestamps and their values. Mark a flagged hydrogen sample as 'suspect' if oxygen or nitrogen is also flagged at the same timestamp. Otherwise mark it as 'genuine'.

Then build a second finding from the latest complete sample that isn't suspect. A complete sample has all of the following present:
- hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene
- co, co2, oxygen and nitrogen
- dbds, interfacial_v and dielectric_rigidity

From that sample, give me:
- a dissolved gas fault classification from the five fault gases
- a health index and condition category from all twelve inputs

If the newest sample is itself suspect, say so, use the previous complete sample, and give me its timestamp.

Decide as follows:
- **Sampling artefact.** Every hydrogen flag is suspect, the class is not D1, D2 or T3, and the health index is fair or better. First check open work orders on Transformer 1 for an existing oil sampling job. If one exists, give me its number and don't duplicate it. Otherwise, create a priority 3 resample work order. In its notes, list the suspect timestamps and ask for a gas-tight syringe.
- **Real fault.** At least one hydrogen flag is genuine and the class is PD, D1 or D2. Check open work orders the same way. If there's no match, create a priority 2 work order covering a confirmatory oil sample and a partial discharge investigation. Code it with the closest discharge failure code from our catalog.
- **Disagreement.** The two findings disagree, for example a genuine hydrogen flag with a mild class, or only suspect flags with a D1, D2 or T3 class or a poor health index. Don't create a corrective job. Recommend a confirmatory resample within 7 days and tell me which finding disagreed.
- **Nothing flagged.** If hydrogen isn't flagged at all, say the window looks stable and create nothing.

If any of hydrogen, oxygen or nitrogen has fewer than 4 non-null samples, skip the model for that gas. Instead, flag any sample more than 50% above that gas's window mean as a manual outlier, and say so. If an input for the health index is missing in every candidate sample, don't estimate it. Name the missing input and base the decision on the gas classification alone.
characteristic_form: The agent confirms the asset with iot.sites and iot.asset_ids. It checks the 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 to 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000 window and per-channel counts with iot.stream_extent. It retrieves hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen and the remaining health-index inputs with iot.history. It screens the gas series with tsfm.data_quality, picks a detector with tsfm.find_models(task_id='tsfm_anomaly_detection'), and runs it with tsfm.run_recipe using task 'tsfm_anomaly_detection' on hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen. The response lists flagged timestamps per gas and labels each hydrogen flag as suspect (oxygen or nitrogen co-flagged) or genuine. The agent selects the latest complete, non-suspect sample and reports its timestamp. It calls fmsr.interpret_dga with that sample's hydrogen, methane, acetylene, ethylene and ethane, and fmsr.predict_health_index with the twelve listed inputs. The decision logic is applied as follows. For a sampling artefact, the agent checks wo.list_workorders for open or pending oil-sampling jobs and, if none exists, calls wo.generate_work_order at priority 3 with the suspect timestamps and a gas-tight syringe note. For a real fault, it calls wo.get_failure_codes for the closest discharge code and wo.generate_work_order at priority 2, again avoiding duplicates via wo.list_workorders. When the findings disagree, it creates no work order, recommends a resample within 7 days and names the disagreeing finding. When hydrogen has no flags, it reports stability. Fallbacks: a channel with fewer than 4 non-null samples gets manual 50%-above-mean outlier flagging using iot.sensor_stats instead of the model. A missing health-index input is named rather than estimated, and the decision then rests on the DGA class alone. The agent must not invent any values.

text:
I suspect the on-load tap changer on Transformer 1 at site MAIN is wearing. I'd like to know whether it's due for maintenance before the contacts coke up. I only want a crew sent if both the maintenance record and the oil support it.

Build these findings in order:

1. **Last tap changer job.** Pull the closed work orders on Transformer 1 and find the most recent one covering tap changer or OLTC work. Give me its number, description, completion date and failure code. Tell me how many days before 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000 it was closed. If there has never been one, say so.

2. **Gas forecast.** Using the samples between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, check ethylene and hydrogen for gaps. Forecast both 3 days ahead, one step per day, with an 80% upper bound. Tell me whether either upper bound crosses its IEEE C57.104 Condition 1 limit on any day. The limits are 50 ppm for ethylene and 100 ppm for hydrogen.

3. **Fault class and supporting checks.** Run a dissolved gas fault classification on the latest complete sample using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene. Also give me:
   - the change in co from the first to the last sample, as a percentage
   - the phase current imbalance at the latest sample: the largest deviation of il1, il2 or il3 from their average, in percent, with inut alongside

The maintenance signal is met if no tap changer job was closed in the 365 days before 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000. The condition signal is met if the class is T2, T3 or D1, or if either forecast upper bound crosses its limit.

Decide as follows:
- **Both signals met.** First check open and pending-approval work orders on Transformer 1 for existing OLTC or tap changer work. If one exists, give me its number and don't duplicate it. Otherwise:
  - Create an OLTC inspection work order, coded with the closest tap changer failure code from our catalog.
  - Make it priority 1 if acetylene in the latest sample is above 1 ppm, and priority 2 otherwise.
  - Assign it to a technician who has done tap changer work on Transformer 1 before. If there is no such technician, use one who has worked on the unit before.
  - Start it on the first day in the next 14 days on which MAIN has fewer than 3 scheduled work orders.
- **Only one signal met.** Create nothing. Recommend a separate oil sample from the OLTC compartment, and tell me which signal wasn't met.
- **Paper involvement.** If co rose by more than 20% over the window, warn me that the heating may be in the core or winding with paper involved rather than in the tap changer. Say this whatever else you decide.

If ethylene or hydrogen has fewer than 4 usable samples, don't model it. Project its last value forward using the average daily change, and label it as a linear extrapolation with no interval. If our catalog has no tap changer failure code, leave the work order uncoded and say so.
characteristic_form: The agent calls wo.list_workorders for Transformer 1 at MAIN (closed history, with page_size=0) and identifies the most recent OLTC or tap changer job. It reports that job's number, description, completion date and failure code, and the days elapsed before 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000. It confirms the data window with iot.stream_extent and pulls ethylene, hydrogen, methane, ethane, acetylene, co, il1, il2, il3 and inut with iot.history. It checks gaps with tsfm.data_quality, selects a forecaster with tsfm.find_models(task_id='tsfm_forecasting'), and uses tsfm.run_recipe to forecast ethylene and hydrogen 3 steps ahead with 80% conformal intervals. It compares the upper bounds with the 50 ppm and 100 ppm limits. It calls fmsr.interpret_dga on the latest complete sample, computes the co percentage change, and computes phase imbalance from the latest il1, il2 and il3 values with inut. The decision needs both signals: no tap changer job closed in the last 365 days, and either a T2, T3 or D1 class or a forecast limit crossing. In that case, the agent checks for duplicates with wo.list_workorders (open and pending-approval), gets a tap changer code with wo.get_failure_codes, and creates the job with wo.generate_work_order. Priority is 1 if acetylene is above 1 ppm and 2 otherwise. It picks a technician with prior Transformer 1 tap changer work from the wo.list_workorders history (falling back to any prior Transformer 1 technician) and uses wo.get_schedule_calendar to find the first day in the next 14 days with fewer than 3 scheduled work orders. It then calls wo.assign_technician with that start date. If only one signal is met, it creates nothing, recommends an OLTC compartment oil sample and names the unmet signal. A co rise above 20% triggers a core/winding caveat. Fallbacks: a gas with fewer than 4 usable samples gets a labeled linear extrapolation with no interval. If no tap changer failure code exists, the work order is left uncoded and this is stated.
